title: Fixed-scalar finite Tate presentations and root-normalized comparisons
statement: Fix a prime $\ell$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ and $n\geq0$. Set $A=\mathcal O_E/\varpi_E^{n+1}$ using [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension], and use its universe lift for fixed-scalar module sheaves. For a scheme $T$, let $L_T=\varprojlim_{s\geq1}\mu_{\ell^s,T}^{\mathrm{pro}}$ be the specified root limit and let $A_T^{\mathrm{pro}}(k)$ be the original finite Tate twist of [def-coefficient-twists-detailed] for $k\geq0$. Define its fixed-scalar presentation by restriction of scalars along the canonical identification of the finite coefficient ring sheaf with the constant ring sheaf: on sections its additive groups and restrictions are unchanged. Define the pure section $g_1(a,x)$ to be the image of $x\otimes a$ under the two scalar-extension sheafification units defining this original twist. Put $g_0(a)=a$ through the constant-sheaf unit and recursively $g_{k+1}(a;x_1,\ldots,x_{k+1})=g_k(a;x_1,\ldots,x_k)\otimes g_1(1,x_{k+1})$ for $k\geq1$. For every $r\geq0$ with $\ell^{r+1}A=0$, use the etale twists $B_{r,T}(k)=(\mu_{\ell^{r+1},T}^{\mathrm{et}}\otimes_{\mathbf Z/\ell^{r+1}}A_T)^{\otimes k}$ of [def-asd-finite-etale-tate-twist], with $B_{r,T}(0)=A_T$, and their analogously defined pure sections $e_k(a;z_1,\ldots,z_k)$. Tensor sections here mean the images of section tensors under sheafification [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product]. Let $p_r(x)$ be the actual unit obtained by projecting $x\in L_T(W)$ to its $\ell^{r+1}$-root and applying the kernel inclusion; let $v(z)$ be the actual unit underlying an etale root. The limit and kernel are those of [def-pur-sheaf-inverse-limit] and [def-pur-roots-of-unity-sheaf]. With the site comparison $\nu_T$ of [def-weil-pbc-site-comparison-morphism], define the following predicates, without asserting existence of an isomorphism. A comparison $b:\nu_T^*B_{r,T}(k)\simeq A_T^{\mathrm{pro}}(k)$ is root-normalized if for every etale $U$, pro-etale $W$, arrow $f:W\to U$, $a\in A$, roots $z_i\in\mu_{\ell^{r+1}}(U)$ and $x_i\in L_T(W)$ with $p_r(x_i)=f^*v(z_i)$, it takes the restriction along $f$ of the comparison-unit image of $e_k(a;z_i)$ to $g_k(a;x_i)$. For every scheme morphism $h:T'\to T$, use the etale and pro-etale inverse images, the latter from [def-weil-proetale-inverse-image]. The declarations are extracted from the existing finite Tate descent module [lem-amb-finite-tate-site-descent]; this citation records the source module for the definitions, not the descent theorem conclusion. An etale pullback isomorphism $c:h^*B_{r,T}(k)\simeq B_{r,T'}(k)$ is normalized if its adjunct sends $e_k(a;z_i)$ to $e_k(a;z'_i)$ on the base-changed object whenever $v(z'_i)$ is the pullback of $v(z_i)$. A pro-etale pullback isomorphism $d:h^*A_T^{\mathrm{pro}}(k)\simeq A_{T'}^{\mathrm{pro}}(k)$ is normalized if its adjunct sends $g_k(a;x_i)$ to $g_k(a;x'_i)$ whenever every $p_s(x'_i)$ is the pullback of $p_s(x_i)$. Finally, for annihilating exponents indexed by $r,r'\geq0$, an exponent-transition isomorphism $t:B_{r',T}(k)\simeq B_{r,T}(k)$ is normalized if it sends $e_k(a;z'_i)$ to $e_k(a;z_i)$ whenever $v(z_i)=v(z'_i)^{\ell^{\max(r'-r,0)}}$. These definitions include $k=0$ and $n=0$ and impose no invertibility, ramification-divisibility, or existence hypothesis.
